analysis:
Reviewed the supplied base_text units of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1638-2205). The PR changes only this documentation file. The visible patch excerpt is truncated. It adds a Qwen-family empty closed think-block seed (kill switch DARKBLOOM_TTFT_THINK_CONTENT_SEED=0), and a 'Streamed auto tool calls' section describing streamToolCallDeltas, ToolStreamPreparation.makeHandler and ToolCallProcessor streaming options for auto tool_choice.

The supplied units are base-side context only and cover neither changed range (head 1493-1505, 1553-1586). No executable code, wire contract or key/attestation behavior changes in the visible evidence, so I found no regression against T-041, TB-002, TB-007 or related threats.

Open questions for deeper review. First, the real source changes behind these doc claims are not supplied (ThinkSeed/parser logic, ToolStreamPreparation, ToolCallProcessor, MLXOpenAIService). Streaming partial tool-call argument fragments could bypass the complete-frame validation that the base docs describe elsewhere (e.g. ToolConstraintValidation). The truncated patch cannot show whether post-hoc validation is preserved for streamed deltas. Second, I could not confirm that the seeded content state does not change reasoning/content separation in a way that leaks reasoning text. Third, the streamed output is encrypted by the provider back over the coordinator connection, so T-008's fail-closed encryption behavior should be checked in the code PR. No security-relevant claims in the visible base text (media accounting, MiMo ownership, prefix cache) were altered by the supplied excerpt. Because the head content is truncated and the code is unseen, I am flagging deeper review.
